sources.citation: Hammarstrom, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212. Sec. 2.4.19 'Walio [ppq, tww, wla, ybx]' and Table (Pei ppq: 'Short wordlist').
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology. States the documentation status: 'There are published wordlists in Conrad & Dye 1975 and in Conrad & Lewis 1988, numerals in Lean 1986, and some very minimal notes on grammar in Laycock & Z'Graggen 1975 (752-753) and Laycock 1973 (32-33).' Table: Pei -- 'Short wordlist'. Confirms in print (as of 2010) that no phonological description of any Walio-family language existed.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. n.d. [uploaded 2010]. Pei Swadesh List. archive.org item rosettaproject_ppq_swadesh-1.
sources.note: c.70 phonetically transcribed forms (e.g. hosaφo 'house', tʰiφo 'head'); no stress marks, no source named, no prose.

sources.note: Pai appears only in Ross's note that pronoun data exist for Papi, Walio and Pai; no phonology.

Documentation 13). Berlin/New York: Mouton de Gruyter. DOI 10.1515/9783110819724. [held page-text, 1903 PDF pages]
sources.note: No stress/tone statement. One sentence: 'Some of the Pai-speakers living at Pai also learned it' (the Hauna trade language); Pai classed with Walio in the Leonard Schultze family.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & Ron Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 243-273. Sec. 4.1 'Leonhard Schultze stock/family' pp.247-248; sociolinguistic notes on Pai c. p.255; Appendix 9.2 wordlists.
sources.note: Nothing (0 hits for stress/accent/tone in the whole paper). Pai: c.80 speakers resettled at Pei village, Pei 1-Pei 2 lists 94% cognate, trade language Yahapiri; the printed wordlist appendix has no Pai column.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert & Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 1-35. Sec. 3.6 'Leonard Schultze and Frieda Rivers'.
sources.note: Pai/Pei not treated at all (only Walio, Paupe, Yabio cognate percentages); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, D.C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Sec. 2.11.3.2 'Leonhard Schultze sub-phylum-level family', pp.752-753; phylum feature list p.732.
sources.note: Nothing for Pai; section gives only noun-classification examples from Pai. The phylum-wide typological list (p.732) includes 'lack of complex suprasegmental systems', not attributed to any Leonhard Schultze language.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. Entry 112 'Pai', pp.32-33; Leonhard Schultze sub-phylum note p.32.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives villages, population 208, sources (Laycock test list DCL71, Basel list, Dye & Townsends 1969) and adjective/classifier examples (ho fawi-sapo 'big house'); no phonology.

sources.citation: Dye, Wayne, Patricia Townsend & William Townsend. 1969 [1968]. The Sepik Hill languages: a preliminary report. Oceania 39(2): 146-156.
sources.note: Catalog has no record and no existing statement for peii1238; this work adds nothing on stress. It does confirm the language's identity and location (Pai, c. 100 speakers, hills between the Leonard Schultze and Wogamus Rivers, member of the Walio/Pai/Yabio/Tuwari family) and is the source Laycock 1973 cites as 'Dye & Townsends 1969' for Pai.

sources.citation: Wichmann, Soren, Eric W. Holman & Cecil H. Brown (eds.). The ASJP Database. Wordlist 'Pei' (doculect PEI; ISO 639-3 ppq, Glottolog peii1238; -4.42, 142.25; 200 speakers), compiled by Matthew S. Dryer from: Laycock, Don. n.d. Notebook D33 (Papi, Walio, Sanio, Pai/Pei), PARADISEC DL2-042. Leipzig: MPI-EVA. 63 concept lines in ASJPcode.
sources.note: Bare 40-item-style Swadesh wordlist (63 lines, e.g. 1 I atareya, 2 you mbEtareya, 11 one gab3geyi, 93 hot heipo tapo, 94 cold helito/b3lEtito) in ASJPcode, which does not encode stress or tone; no stress marks, no prose, no phonology notes. Wordlist-only data, not a statement. Its value is as a pointer: it confirms Laycock's Notebook D33 contains a usable Pai list and that Dryer has worked through it.
